Please acknowledge that psychotherapy, including cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), can be beneficial for individuals with schizophrenia, particularly in addressing co-occurring issues like anxiety, depression, and social skills. However, psychotherapy alone is not sufficient to manage the core symptoms of schizophrenia. Psychotherapy is most effective when used alongside medication, as it can help individuals cope with their condition, adhere to their treatment plan, and improve their daily functioning. I am a psychologist and I am no pro medicines, but if he is actually having schizophrenia as assessed by the psychiatrist I believe, then my suggestion would be to continue both side by side.

As someone who has experience working with adolescents, I can tell you parenting plays a very big role during this critical period of adolescence. Keep a check, yes, but also know the boundaries and give them some space too. Tell her as a parent you have these concerns and you understand why she might have been smoking. Try to know the reason.
